original_test_intent: Install the approved DOCA host repository, runtime, SDK and tools, then verify the intended BlueField DPU identity and host driver/firmware state match recipe; any BFB/firmware flash is separately governed.
original_method: Pin signed repo/package versions/checksums/license and host OS/kernel compatibility; identify DPU serial/BDF/SKU and recipe; capture package/services/network/PCIe baseline and recovery; preserve logs; approve apt/dpkg changes, install allowlisted packages with complete logs, run MST/lspci/devlink, compare versions/ID and reboot only if explicitly required; flash only under separate authorization.
manual_activity: Host/DPU owner supplies signed repo/package recipe and chooses install/reboot/flash boundary; operator protects networking, workloads and OOB and owns package/firmware recovery.
required_inputs: Host OS/kernel/arch and package dependency compatibility
BlueField serial/BDF/SKU and expected device/driver/firmware recipe
Trusted repository and pinned package manifest
Separate signed BFB/firmware artifact only if independently approved
safety_requirements: Do not conflate host packages with DPU flash
Do not install sshpass solely for automation
Maintain OOB/redundant power and network recovery
Stop on dependency/device/network/PCIe anomaly; no auto-retry
agent_execution_scope: Capture baseline and install allowlisted host packages
Perform reboot or flash only under separate exact approval

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its BFB flash/reboot expansion exceeds the source and its sshpass/head pipeline truncates evidence; only read-only postchecks may be reused after approval.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use pinned dpkg/apt package manifests with captured logs, then full MST/lspci/devlink output; handle BFB/firmware separately.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: DOCA host installation, listed dependencies, 15-minute allocations and device-ID-to-SPEC verification are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat host package installation as a version-locked transaction with dependency diff, service/network checks and rollback; isolate any DPU firmware activation as another change.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds artifact trust, package manifest, target mapping, evidence and recovery while removing credential-risk dependency.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only connection checks or an unapproved flash cannot substitute for verified host installation.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Package changes can alter dependencies/network services; wrong BFB/firmware can strand DPU or host.

project_override_considerations: Networking/DPU owner must decide exact DOCA package set, whether reboot is required, expected MST/devlink versions and whether firmware/BFB remains explicitly out of this row.
expected_evidence: Artifact/repo signatures/checksums and pinned package manifest
Host/DPU identity/recipe and pre/post package/service state
Full MST/lspci/devlink outputs and SPEC comparison
Rollback/reboot/flash record if separately approved and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master performs host DOCA package installation and MST identity checks, while DeepSeek asserts DPU firmware/BFB flashing and reboot as if intrinsic; those scopes and risks are materially different.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; execution blocks if signed artifacts, host/DPU mapping, authoritative install/flash scope, package trust, rollback or OOB cannot be established.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row383 Wistron-Networking-00372-V003: approve source host-only DOCA repo/runtime/SDK/tools scope versus separately authorized BFB/firmware flash/reboot; provide signed package versions/checksums, host compatibility, BlueField serial/BDF/SKU recipe, exact device/version oracle, package/network rollback, OOB/power and reboot semantics.

review_improvement: Separates a routine-but-stateful host software install from a much riskier DPU flash and preserves complete version/identity evidence for both boundaries.
independent_technical_reasoning: Installing DOCA host packages can change dependencies and services without changing DPU firmware, whereas BFB flashing mutates the DPU and often needs reboot/recovery. Treating them as one step obscures both coverage and blast radius; each target and version transition must be independently identified and authorized.
